reason: Premises 1–4 are directly supported by the cited evidence (E1, E2) from the same 2022 paper, which reports the exact grain size, dislocation density, hardness/toughness improvements, and oxidation resistance for UHPS ZrB2. Premise 5 (liquid metal corrosion durability) is not addressed in the cited passages; it is an extrapolation without specific prior evidence.
premises: UHPS at 15 GPa/1450 °C refines ZrB2 grain size to ~0.7 µm and raises dislocation density to ~1.7×10^15 m⁻²
Dislocation engineering simultaneously improves hardness (~46%) and fracture toughness (~69%) in UHPS ZrB2
UHPS ZrB2 exhibits excellent oxidation resistance due to nano-sized subgrains forming a protective oxide
Plastic deformation under ultra-high pressure is the dominant densification mechanism, enabling full density at low temperature
These microstructural and property enhancements will translate to improved durability in liquid metal plating environments
